source: NCERT Class XII, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Ch. 5 (Primary Activities).

sections.heading: 1. Economic Activities — Classification
points: Economic activities are grouped into **primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary**.
**Primary activities** = directly dependent on the **environment** — extracting/producing from nature.
They include **hunting-gathering, pastoralism, fishing, forestry, mining, and agriculture**.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Farming
points: **Subsistence agriculture** — for the farmer's own needs: **primitive (shifting/slash-and-burn — jhum, milpa, ladang)** and **intensive subsistence** (dense populations, small plots, e.g. rice in monsoon Asia).
**Commercial agriculture** — for the market: **commercial grain farming, mixed farming, dairy, plantation, and Mediterranean agriculture**.
**Plantation agriculture** — single cash crop (tea, coffee, rubber) on large estates.

sections.heading: 3. Pastoralism, Mining and Gathering
points: **Nomadic herding (pastoral nomadism)** — moving with animals in search of pasture (dry/cold regions).
**Commercial livestock rearing** — organised ranching (large scale, for market).
**Mining** — extraction of minerals; depends on the **richness (grade) of ore, method (surface/underground), and accessibility**.
**Gathering** — collecting forest produce (in tropical/high latitude forests).

sections.heading: 4. Modern Commercial Farming
points: **Extensive commercial grain farming** — wheat/maize on large farms (prairies, steppes) with machinery.
**Dairy farming** — near urban markets; highly capital/labour intensive.
**Mixed farming** — crops + livestock together.
**Market gardening / horticulture** ('truck farming') — vegetables/fruits/flowers for cities.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Primary = directly dependent on nature (farming, mining, fishing, forestry).
Shifting cultivation = jhum (India), milpa (Mexico), ladang (SE Asia).
Plantation = single cash crop (tea/coffee/rubber) on large estates.
Nomadic herding vs commercial ranching; mining depends on ore grade + accessibility.
Market gardening = 'truck farming' (vegetables/fruits for cities).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Mining and agriculture are primary activities** (nature-dependent).
**Shifting cultivation** = slash-and-burn (jhum/milpa/ladang).
**Plantation agriculture** grows a **single** cash crop on large estates.
**Market gardening** (truck farming) supplies **fresh produce to cities**.
